content.content: Can you help with two things at once? 1) Calculate the final velocity of a car that starts at 20 m/s, accelerates at 2 m/s² for 15 seconds. 2) Also, find the number of ways 4 books can be arranged out of a set of 10.
{"result": 50.0}
{"result": 5040}

Here are your results:

1) The final velocity of the car is 50.0 m/s after accelerating for 15 seconds.
2) There are 5,040 ways to arrange 4 books out of a set of 10.
Now, tell me the final velocity if the car starts at 0 m/s but the other values remain the same. And calculate the arrangements if we want to arrange all 10 books.
{"result": 30.0}

With an initial velocity of 0 m/s, the car's final velocity after 15 seconds at 2 m/s² acceleration is 30.0 m/s.
For arranging all 10 books, there are 3,628,800 possible permutations.
What if we only had 6 books and wanted to arrange 6 of them? Also, what would the final velocity be if time was 5 seconds instead?
{"result": 720}
{"result": 10.0}
If you arrange all 6 books, there are 720 ways to do so. With an initial velocity of 0 m/s and acceleration of 2 m/s² for 5 seconds, the final velocity is 10.0 m/s.
How many ways can you arrange 3 of the 6 books? And what is the velocity if you accelerate for 30 seconds from 0 m/s?
{"result": 120}
{"result": 60.0}
You can arrange 3 of the 6 books in 120 different ways. If you accelerate from 0 m/s for 30 seconds at 2 m/s², the final velocity is 60.0 m/s.
Try with 6 books, arranging only 1. And with the car scenario, what is the velocity after 1 second from the same initial conditions?
{"result": 6}
{"result": 2.0}
<finish> There are 6 ways to arrange just 1 book out of 6. After accelerating from 0 m/s for 1 second at 2 m/s², the car's final velocity is 2.0 m/s. </finish>
